decisions.decided: Lane holds a plugin with several skills that each start a run of their own: each skill's run is held to that skill's steps and routes, as a plugin with several commands is common and a skill left unheld raises KR1.1

decisions.about: Runs of several skills in one conversation
decisions.decided: the runs of several skills of one plugin go on side by side in one conversation, each held to its own skill's steps and routes: each Start records the skill whose run started it, a subagent's events go to its Start's run by agent_id, a result goes to the skill it names, and the main conversation's start goes to the run whose due start it matches, as a person typing another command while a background subagent works is common use, and a plugin that refuses it doesn't run as its maker designed, which raises KR1.1

decisions.about: How the run record is kept
decisions.decided: the run record keeps only the facts no payload gives again: each Start let through with the skill whose run started it, its tie to an agent_id, and each Result; each hook process adds them as lines and never rewrites one, and the guard works out where each run stands from those lines on each event; what a payload carries each time, such as session_id, agent_type, and the skill a result names, is read from the payload and never kept, as hooks of parallel subagents run at once and a rewritten or derived value kept goes stale or loses another's update, which raises KR1.1

decisions.about: What the kept-results adapter is given
decisions.decided: the guard gives the plugin's kept-results adapter the words typed after the command, or the Skill tool's args, which the hook event carries, so that the plugin alone decides from them whether the call starts a run or picks one up, as a plugin whose command takes a request needs to tell the two apart and no part of the plugin is asked before the guard

decisions.about: How the guard tells each hook event apart
decisions.decided: the architecture says, from the records, how the guard tells which run, Start, and role each hook event belongs to: a run by session_id, a Start and its role by agent_id, the main conversation by an event with no agent_id, and a Start tied to its agent_id at the PostToolUse of its Agent call; it does so for the states that the README's main use and rn bring about, and gives each rare state one line that names what Lane does there, never holding a call to another run's rules, as Lane's purpose needs no more

the checks that lay.py writes into the plugin hold from the prompt after the person types /reload-plugins, which lay.py write asks for, as Claude Code loads a plugin's hooks only as a session starts or on that command, and no conversation can reload itself; an AI that lays asks whoever gives its conversation the prompts

its Test strategy, by the architecture best practice, decides each level's tools and each quality check with its criterion, and every test case is written in test code before any implementation, as the architecture best practice's node decides
Test strategy holds a compatibility test: on each new Claude Code version, the recorder scripts run each recorded state again, and what Claude Code gives is compared with what the test double gives

decisions.about: The test double of Claude Code
decisions.decided: the double gives each event as the records show it: a prompt_id that changes within a turn, the prompt_id of a notification, SubagentStart before the PostToolUse of its Agent call, the order of a foreground subagent's events, a subagent started by a subagent, and a queued SendMessage that resumes a subagent

decisions.about: Where the list of Claude Code's states lies
decisions.decided: the states of Claude Code that the guard meets, each with the events it sends and the records that show it, lie in a file of their own that the architecture links, as they change with each Claude Code version while the architecture holds only what stays true

the user signs off the plan, the goal and the deliverables with their decisions, before rn makes anything, and each deliverable once its evaluators find it good, before the next rests on it. The last sign-off marks the draft pull request ready, and the merge stays the user's
/rn:up starts a run and picks one up, /rn:dn pauses it, /rn:ty approves the sign-off waiting, and /rn:gm sends it back with the user's words or their comments on the pull request, Done included

/rn:dn stops each role at once and commits and pushes its work so far with the step it was on. /rn:up, in any conversation or on another computer, goes on from that step, and shows where it stopped, what comes next, and the point or sign-off waiting. A run closed without /rn:dn goes back only to its last step, as rn keeps its state at the end of each step

what the evaluators found the people can do with the deliverable, the decisions taken without asking, and a link to its changes in the pull request. /rn:gm alone takes every comment the user wrote on the pull request since the sign-off
rn works in a git worktree of its own on the work's branch, so the user goes on with their own work while rn runs
once the rebuilt rn exists, the maker follows its install steps from nothing as a newcomer would, and mends the README where they fall short
